independence_basis: separate process, fresh session, clean checkout, integrity verified

findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R3/probe_restore.py: implementer writes 'ref: refs/heads/other' (then 'ref: refs/heads/canon', the main checkout's branch) into its own worktree git dir HEAD and edits a file. worktree_identity() still passes (gitfile untouched). do_repair: head != sha -> TAMPER reason -> _restore() -> `git reset --hard <sha>` updates the symbolic ref. Result: branch 'other' moved 1077e67 -> b097513 (candidate), its commit dropped; second run: 'canon' (checked out in main repo) moved a839efc -> c097ed5 and the main checkout shows 'D pkg/feature.py'. repair.json records restored=True while impl HEAD is refs/heads/other|canon, not the candidate branch. R2-03's class (revert not limited to the implementation worktree) persists via this sibling vector.
findings.suggested_fix: Before resetting, require `git symbolic-ref HEAD` == refs/heads/<candidate.branch> (else TAMPER, no reset); restore with `update-ref refs/heads/<branch> <sha> <expected-old>` + `symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/<branch>` + `reset --hard` / `clean -fd`, and include the HEAD symref in the restored check and in the review integrity snapshot.
findings.title: Revert after a refused repair resets whatever branch the implementation worktree's HEAD names: a redirected HEAD makes the driver move another branch (incl. the main checkout's) to the candidate SHA

findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R3/probe_cache.py (A): baseline-only transient hang -> run1 BLOCKED 'baseline gate slow: TIMED_OUT'; cause removed, owner unblock, run2 BLOCKED with the identical reason; state baseline_gates.slow.result.status == 'TIMED_OUT'. The cache is reused whenever key matches regardless of status; editing state.json to clear it is TAMPER. Same path for exit-75 GPU lease busy on the baseline (R2-05), contradicting 'provide the resource and re-run'.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache baseline results only when status == COMPLETED_WITH_RESULT (or re-run when the cached status is not), recording each attempt as a BASELINE_GATE event.
findings.title: A non-COMPLETED baseline gate result (TIMED_OUT, GPU lease busy, BLOCKED) is cached by SHA+cmd and permanently blocks qualification

findings.evidence: Probe probe_cache.py (B): run to VERIFIED (BLOCKED OWNER_AUTHORIZATION), commit to the candidate branch outside the driver, then unblock+run three times: each run goes READY_TO_RESUME -> VERIFYING -> gates -> evidence_ok fails -> BLOCKED 'no independent ACCEPT on this exact commit' with resume_to VERIFYING again; rounds stays 1, verify() == []. The 'needs: re-audit' remedy is unreachable (L-AC14 liveness).
findings.suggested_fix: When the candidate changed or the blocker is EVIDENCE (no accepted review for the current SHA), set resume_to=AUDITING; generally resume to AUDITING whenever accepted_review(current sha) is None.
findings.title: Candidate moved during VERIFYING/VERIFIED blocks with resume_to=VERIFYING, so every resume re-blocks and the new commit is never re-audited

findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R3/probe_config.py: candidate changes protected core/frozen.py; run1 -> WAITING_FOR_MODEL (reviewer unavailable). Config file edited between runs (authorized_protected_changes ['core/**'], gates []) - the file sits outside every integrity check, writable by implementer/reviewer/escaped child or coordinator. run2 -> COMPLETE, protected change pushed to the bare canonical remote; only a CONFIG_CHANGED event; verify() == []. Under the original config this stops BLOCKED (OWNER_DECISION) (L-AC11/L-AC12).
findings.suggested_fix: Bind the config hash in the PLAN event; on a changed config block (OWNER_DECISION/CONFIG) until `unblock --note` acknowledges it, and record the policy-relevant fields in the chain; consider keeping authorisation flags out of the agent-written config.
findings.title: Milestone policy (protected-path authorisation, gates, integration authorisation, reviewer) is re-read every run; a changed config is only logged, so any writer can relax policy mid-milestone

findings.evidence: Unkeyed SHA-256 chain: appending a REVIEW_RECORDED event (independent true, ACCEPT, matching round_sha256) plus STAGE VERIFYING, with the same history/rounds entries in state.json and a rounds/R<n>/round.json, satisfies accepted_review() and verify() (code-read; no rewrite of existing events needed). Doc says 'whoever can rewrite the whole state directory', and §6 says setsid children's 'later writes are caught by the clean-worktree checks', which is false for state_dir and config writes. Nothing anchors the chain on resume.
findings.suggested_fix: State precisely that any process able to write state_dir can append a forged independent ACCEPT; owner decision on an external anchor (e.g. committed chain head checked on resume, or key/isolation outside the worker/coordinator's reach).
findings.title: Docs understate state-forging: an append-only forge suffices, and setsid-escaped worker writes outside the worktree are not caught

A: baseline TIMED_OUT cached, still BLOCKED after cause removed + unblock; B: moved candidate loops VERIFYING->BLOCKED, rounds stays 1
